reason: The hypothesis directly restates the well-known contrast between Al/Si (protective) and Mn (non-protective) oxidation behavior in CrFeCoNi-based HEAs, as reported in multiple passages (P1, P2, P8, P24, P25, P30, P31, P33, P35, P36). The mechanism of diffusion-controlled oxide growth and the predicted outcomes are taken almost verbatim from these sources, with no new alloy, regime, or mechanistic integration beyond what is already established.
copied_elements: Exposing CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C in oxidative atmosphere
X = Al or Si forms protective Al2O3 or SiO2 scales
X = Mn forms thick, mixed Mn-rich oxides and spinels prone to cracking and spallation
Mn's fast outward diffusion and high reactivity cause non-protective oxide formation
Al and Si lower oxygen permeability and slow outward diffusion
Comparison of Al/Si vs. Mn alloys under identical high-temperature oxidation
Falsification by checking if Al/Si alloys show thinner, more coherent, adherent scales vs. Mn alloy
